title: Slot-based maintenance windows with SLO-aware drain reservations for Dedicated fleets
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Problem: Maintenance and upgrades on Dedicated fleets today cause unpredictable throughput variability for customers with throughput guarantees. Ad-hoc rolling drains and coarse autoscaler reactions can temporarily breach SLOs for latency/throughput-sensitive tenants.

Goal: Implement a slot-based maintenance window system that reserves 'throughput tokens' per maintenance slot, ties drain behavior to SLO-aware thresholds, and coordinates with the autoscaler and routing layer to preserve committed throughput contracts during maintenance. The system should: preserve tenant throughput guarantees where possible, make maintenance impact predictable, allow safe parallelism across non-conflicting slots, and provide observable dashboards and rollback controls.

High-level approach:
- Define maintenance "slots" (time-bound, capacity-limited windows) assigned to node groups. Each slot exposes a fixed number of throughput tokens (a soft capacity reservation) that the scheduler honors when initiating drains.
- SLO-aware drain thresholds: before draining a node that hosts guaranteed-throughput tenants, evaluate current per-tenant token usage vs reservations; if draining would drop a tenant below its reservation, the drain is delayed or the tenant is proactively migrated to a standby host using capacity from the slot.
- Autoscaler integration: slots communicate with the autoscaler to request temporary burst capacity or cross-fleet buffer pools; autoscaler makes short-lived scale decisions constrained by defined budget.
- Fleet controls + routing: smart routing will preferentially route guaranteed tenants away from drains and into warmed-backed replicas; fallback policies allow best-effort tenants to be deprioritized during slot maintenance.
- Observability: per-slot dashboards (Console) showing reserved tokens, active drains, expected SLO impact, and a simulator for planned windows.

Acceptance criteria:
1) Orchestrator can schedule and run a maintenance slot for a small test cluster preserving >=95% of committed throughput for affected tenants under synthetic load.
2) Drains target only nodes within the assigned slot; SLO-aware delays are exercised and logged.
3) Autoscaler accepts temporary burst requests and honors the budget cap.
4) Console shows per-slot forecast and real-time metrics; on-call can cancel a slot with a single action.

Non-goals: full multi-region cross-fleet contract rebalancing in v1; support for every weird tenancy packing case.

Security and compliance notes: slot metadata contains tenant IDs and reservation tokens; all control-plane traffic must be logged and encrypted per Private deployment requirements.

comments: 2025-02-19 - Kickoff: scoped core concepts with Product and SRE. Decided to model tokens as soft reservations rather than hard capacity claims to avoid starvation for bursty tenants. Action: engineering spikes for simulator and API design (owner: Marcus).

2025-02-25 - Spike results: simulator shows that reserving 20% of fleet capacity in a slot reduces maintenance-induced throughput loss from ~40% to ~7% under steady synthetic traffic. Observation: tail latencies still spike if background cache warming is not handled; we need proactive KV warmers. Added to backlog.

2025-03-01 - Design review with PM/Console: Console team asked for a cancel-and-rollback button on each scheduled slot. UX: one-click cancel should trigger drain abort and prioritized reintegration. Marcus to add an api endpoint and reconcile with orchestrator abort semantics. Confluence updated: design link above.

2025-03-03 - Security review stub: initial review flagged slot audit logs must be forwarded to central SIEM. Security asked for field-level encryption of reservation tokens for Private deploys. Owner: Security team to provide KMS hooks. See ticket SEC-1202 (internal).

2025-03-05 - Engineering update: merged initial scheduler API prototype PR #1427 into feature branch. Next: integrate with autoscaler request API (work blocked until ENG-40981 autoscale budgeting PR merges). Testing plan: run slot scheduling on canary fleet next week behind feature flag.

2025-03-05 - QA note: load-sim scenarios updated to include mixed workloads: 70% guaranteed-throughput tenants, 30% best-effort. Test vectors and baseline traces are in the simulation repo. QA owner: Elena Garcia.

Open question: how do we account for multi-tenant nodes where reservation tokens overlap? Proposal: compute a weighted eviction cost and prefer evicting low-cost best-effort shards; need to formalize cost model and run worst-case tests.
